svg.title: Jarvis Disc Mk I speaker and chamber
svg.text: Speaker and chamber: placement, sealed volume, expected response (taller plinth, Dayton CE52N-4)
Volumes are estimates; depth 30.8 is from the maker page, the mounting holes are not listed
A. SECTION THROUGH THE CENTRE: SEALED CHAMBER
sound leaves through the 3 mm gap under the plinth
seals the 24 mm hole in the floor
beside the driver, above the flange
B. PLAN VIEW OF THE PLINTH, LID OFF (FRONT AT THE BOTTOM)
Grey disc = driver flange (52); dashed gold = Ø46 opening in the plinth floor; its mounting holes are not specified in the manufacturer drawing.
Dark green = controller and amp boards on 4 mm pads at r 34, just above the flange; M3 posts at r 38 merge into the neck wall.
minus driver body in the chamber
The cone breathes into the 3 mm gap under the plinth, the back into this chamber.
Fs 164, Qts 0.59, Vas 0.17 L (Dayton spec table)
Qtc 0.7 is flat. This driver gives about 0.79 here: a tiny bump, no EQ needed.
Expect a clean desk speaker down to about 200 Hz: still not a bass speaker.
Xmax is only 0.85 mm: high-pass at 150 Hz in firmware and keep the volume moderate.
D. SPEAKER CHOICE: DAYTON AUDIO CE52N-4 (4 OHM)
2 inch dual-neodymium full range, 4 ohm, 5 W RMS (10 W max), about US$8
Sensitivity 85 dB (2.83 V, 1 m), Re 3.3 ohm, 120 Hz to 20 kHz as rated
Sd 12.6 cm2, Xmax 0.85 mm, Mms 1.3 g, BL 2.5 Tm
Fs 164 Hz, Qts 0.59, Vas 0.17 L: gives Qtc 0.8 in this chamber
Frame 52 mm, baffle cutout 47.5 mm, overall depth 30.8 mm
Mounting hole pattern and flange thickness are not on the maker page: open the spec sheet drawing.
Depth 30.8 leaves 2.7 mm under the neck top; the lift could drop to 15 if you want it shorter.
Parts Express may be out of stock; Sound Imports (EU) lists it. Buy 2 to 3, they are cheap.
Check the cone moves freely before gluing the gasket: it only has 0.85 mm of travel.
SEAL EVERYTHING, THE BOX MUST BE AIRTIGHT
Cable hole in the body floor: foam plug or grommet around the wires
Body-to-neck joint: 1 mm closed-cell foam ring or a bead of silicone
USB-C slot and mute-button hole: silicone or hot glue around the part
Driver flange: 0.5 mm foam gasket, six screws pull it down evenly
Slit under the plinth: 327 mm x 3 mm = about 980 mm2 against a 1260 mm2 cone: close enough. Feet of 4 mm (+1 mm overall) would match it.
jarvis_disc.scad is updated (lift 16.5, round 48 opening (provisional), 4 mm board pads) but the STL files are not re-exported. Regenerate after physical fit validation.
